questions.question: Which two flow directions does a Pipecat pipeline use?
options: DOWNSTREAM (source to sink) and UPSTREAM (feedback, cancel, barge-in)
PUBLISH and SUBSCRIBE, mirroring the Frame-to-FrameProcessor queue design
REQUEST and RESPONSE, matching the STT-to-LLM-to-TTS turn-taking cycle
SYNC and ASYNC, selected per transport to match Daily or LiveKit timing
questions.explanation: Frames flow downstream source-to-sink and upstream for control and cancellation.

questions.question: What is the canonical Pipecat voice pipeline?
options: STT -> VAD -> TTS -> LLM -> transport
VAD -> STT -> LLM -> TTS -> transport
LLM -> STT -> VAD -> TTS -> transport
TTS -> LLM -> VAD -> STT -> transport -> cache
questions.explanation: VAD detects voice activity, STT transcribes, LLM responds, TTS speaks, transport delivers.

questions.question: Which two voice agent classes does LiveKit Agents ship?
options: TelephonyAgent (SIP-only audio) and BrowserAgent (WebRTC-only audio)
ScriptedAgent (fixed dialogue tree) and FreeformAgent (open-ended LLM chat)
MultimodalAgent (direct audio) and VoicePipelineAgent (STT/LLM/TTS cascade)
InboundAgent (receives incoming calls) and OutboundAgent (places outbound calls via SIP)
questions.explanation: MultimodalAgent uses direct audio (Realtime-style); VoicePipelineAgent uses STT->LLM->TTS for text-level control.

questions.question: What is barge-in and how is it handled?
options: An LLM cost spike triggered by long context; the fix is to truncate conversation history
A provider outage on the STT service; the fix is to fail over to a backup transcription vendor immediately
A CAPTCHA failure during telephony SIP setup; the fix is to retry the call after a short delay
The user interrupts while the agent is speaking; UPSTREAM cancel frames stop TTS mid-utterance
questions.explanation: Barge-in is user interruption; UPSTREAM cancellation is how Pipecat handles it cleanly.

questions.question: What end-to-end latency does the lesson describe as premium?
options: About 450-600 ms end-to-end, the premium stack range cited for Vapi and Retell
About 50 ms, roughly the latency of a single VAD frame detection alone
About 1500 ms, the threshold above which the lesson says it starts to feel broken
About 5000 ms, comparable to a slow batch API round trip with retries
questions.explanation: Premium stacks land around 450-600 ms; 800-1200 ms is common; over 1500 ms feels broken.

questions.question: What goes wrong if STT confidence is ignored?
options: Latency improves noticeably because skipping the confidence check removes a processing step from STT
Low-confidence transcripts feed the LLM as if gospel, producing wrong answers; gate on confidence or ask for confirmation
TTS gets faster since it no longer needs to synthesize a spoken confirmation prompt back to the user
Calls get meaningfully cheaper because the pipeline stops requesting extra SIP telephony minutes for repeated retries
questions.explanation: Treating low-confidence STT as truth is a top voice-agent failure mode.
